name: 57. Claude Code turn normalization - assistant prefill trim + mid-conversation system inlining (#6334)
description:
Claude Code sends two shapes that Gemini/Vertex cannot accept verbatim, and until #6334 the Gemini egress
converter (core/providers/gemini/responses.go) normalized neither, so /anthropic/v1/messages traffic pointed at
gemini/vertex failed upstream with HTTP 400.

1. TRAILING ASSISTANT PREFILL. Claude Code routinely ends its messages array with a role:"assistant" turn for the
   model to continue. Bifrost mapped it to a Gemini role:"model" content. Gemini's Content.role is documented as
   "Must be either 'user' or 'model'" and generateContent rejects a history whose final turn is "model"
   ("Please ensure that multiturn requests ends with a user role or a function response"). Gemini exposes no
   prefill mechanism at all, so the turn is trimmed. Bedrock has done this since #3517.

2. MID-CONVERSATION SYSTEM TURN. Claude Code injects runtime state as role:"system" entries inside messages.
   Gemini has no message-level system role, so Bifrost hoisted them into systemInstruction - which renders ahead
   of every message, presenting a turn-40 reminder as though it were said at turn 0, and invalidating the cached
   prefix behind it on every injection. They are now inlined in place as user turns wrapped in
   <system-reminder>, matching convertBifrostSystemReminderToBedrockUserMessage (#4068) and the native Anthropic
   fallback inlineMidConversationSystem.

Every case asserts the OUTBOUND provider payload via x-bf-send-back-raw-request rather than merely checking that
the call did not 400. A "no 400" assertion would pass on a provider that silently tolerated the bad shape and
would tell us nothing about which normalization ran; raw_request pins the converter itself.

FIXTURE CONSTRAINTS - do not "tidy" these bodies:
 - Case B needs TWO consecutive trailing assistant turns. A fix that drops only messages[len-1] passes case A
   and still fails case B.
 - Case E needs a leading top-level `system` AND a later role:"system" entry. Without the leading one the case
   cannot distinguish "inlined correctly" from "system handling dropped entirely".
 - Case G is the anti-over-trim guard: its trailing assistant turn carries tool_use, which is unanswered history
   rather than a prefill and must survive. A trim that keys only on role:"assistant" passes A-C and breaks G.
 - A 400 is NOT guarded away in these scripts - a 400 IS the regression signature here.
